note: modal_page lets you create configurable modal/pop-up dialogs. Each modal is a 'modal' config entity (config_prefix 'modal' => config modal_page.modal.<id>), managed at /admin/structure/modal (entity.modal.collection); global behavior lives in the modal_page.settings config object (form route modal_page.settings = the configure route, at /admin/config/user-interface/modal-page/settings). One permission: 'administer modal page'. Drush: modal_page:cron (alias modal-page-cron) runs ModalPageScheduler. Hooks: hook_modal_alter / hook_modal_ID_alter / hook_modal_submit. Medium cases create a modal / set a known settings value and the agent reads the live config back; hard cases create a modal / configure modal_page.settings, verified against live config. Settings cleanups restore shipped defaults explicitly (State is unreliable on this site). Grounded in src/Entity/Modal.php, modal_page.routing.yml, modal_page.permissions.yml, src/Drush/Commands/ModalPageCommands.php, config/install/modal_page.settings.yml.

evals.prompt: I installed the Drupal 'Modal' (modal_page) module. Where do I go to create a new modal/pop-up, and what kind of Drupal object is each modal?
evals.expected_output: Go to Structure > Modal (/admin/structure/modal, route entity.modal.collection) and click Add Modal. Each modal is a 'modal' config entity, stored as config modal_page.modal.<id>.

evals.prompt: Which permission controls administering the modal_page module, and what is the route/path of its global settings form?
evals.expected_output: The permission is 'administer modal page' (restrict access), which gates all admin routes. The global settings form is route modal_page.settings at /admin/config/user-interface/modal-page/settings (also the module's 'configure' route).

evals.prompt: Does modal_page provide a Drush command (e.g. for scheduling) and any hooks I can implement to alter modals or react to a modal submit?
evals.expected_output: Drush command: modal_page:cron (alias modal-page-cron) runs the scheduler (ModalPageScheduler) to publish/unpublish scheduled modals. Hooks: hook_modal_alter(&$modal, $modal_id), hook_modal_ID_alter(&$modal, $modal_id) and hook_modal_submit($modal, $modal_state, $modal_id).

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a modal (modal_page) with machine id 'mp_known'. Inspect the live modal configuration and tell me which pages/paths it is set to appear on.
evals.expected_output: It shows on /node/* — modal_page.modal.mp_known has pages: '/node/*' (type: page, size modal-lg).

evals.prompt: On this site the modal_page global settings have been customized. Inspect the live modal_page.settings configuration and tell me the configured default cookie expiration value.
evals.expected_output: default_cookie_expiration is 7777 — modal_page.settings.default_cookie_expiration = 7777 (bootstrap_version was also set to 5x).

evals.prompt: Using the modal_page module, create a modal with machine id 'mp_task' and title 'Welcome' that appears on the front page (pages = <front>) and opens automatically. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A modal config entity modal_page.modal.mp_task exists with pages containing <front> and auto_open enabled (truthy).

evals.prompt: Configure the modal_page global settings on this live site: set the Bootstrap version to 5x and the default cookie expiration to 3600. Apply the change.
